name: Whoopee
tagline: You'll jump off almost anything. As long as it was your idea.
epigraph: There's artichoke in this glass. Say so, and people pull a face. Then they taste it.
language_row: Wren's resonance: ready (v2; reaffirmed on v3 in r6). Guest text 4-gram clean against every pour (Wren r3–r6). Gendered pronouns in y1–y3 refer to David Kirke only, accepted by Wren, Hester and Tomás.
sources: Fact cards `_studio/fact-cards/david-kirke-clifton-bungee.md` (all secondary web sources, dated and attributed: NYT, Washington Post and Telegraph obituaries; ITV 2019 via Wayback; *Country Life*, Hay-Nicholls, Nov 2019; Guinness World Records; *Independent* 2023; BBC 2014; *San Francisco Chronicle* archive, 9 Oct 1979) and `sloe-gin.md` (Difford's Guide; Sipsmith; Oxford pdf 1537, 1573, 1814). Drink: *Cocktail Codex* pp. 9, 260; *The Flavor Matrix* pdf 32; Oxford FLOWER-BASED SPIRITS pdf 822; *Proper* p. 68; *Imbibe!* pdf 96, 122; *Liquid Intelligence* p. 131; Woodland Trust (blackthorn). Room notes `work/outlaw-explorer/`.
names_note: Whoopee (Wren; all three, r4–r6): Kirke's own word for the feeling, mildly cheeky. Also considered: On the Understanding, No Backing Out, Brief Moments, Top Hat and Tails, Your Own Idea.
open_items: Not veto-free: generic sloe gin can carry crushed stones or added almond (Difford's, Sipsmith; Sipsmith's own notes say "stone-fruit almond"), so the pour contains nuts. No named bottle states otherwise (Plymouth's page didn't load).
The whole story rests on secondary web sources; the library has nothing on the Clifton jump (Hester).
Sloe gin's sugar (about 20 g/100 ml) is derived from Liquid Intelligence's Blackthorn; Tomás swept 15–30 g, 20–30% and gin 40–47% (48 cases, none OUT).

Kept out: the night of partying and champagne, Hulton's "always terrified", "Kirke always went first", the police watching on family advice (one source), the charge and custody time (sources conflict), the back injury.
Dossier-only coincidence: the blackthorn sprig in blossom and fruit holds April (Clifton) and October (Golden Gate).
